caption: Editor-only assemblies never reach the player, and the arrows only point one way: Assembly-CSharp can reference an asmdef, an asmdef cannot see Assembly-CSharp.
The same value, two routes: through SerializedProperty you get undo, prefab overrides and dirtying for free; writing the field directly gets none of them.
OnPreprocessTexture rewrites the importer settings before the import runs; the bars show why one forgotten setting matters.
Mono defers compilation to the device with a JIT; IL2CPP does all the work at build time, which is why its builds are slow and its players need no JIT.
A type reached only by name through reflection looks unused to the linker; link.xml is what keeps it in the player.
A CI run in batch mode, and why EditMode tests carry most of the load: they take milliseconds where a PlayMode test takes seconds.
The scene points at a GUID, not a path: keep the .meta with the file and the rename is harmless; leave it behind and the GUID changes.
Smart Merge pairs objects by fileID, so both edits survive; a line merge can drop the m_Component entry and orphan the new component.
The agent changes assets only through C# and the Editor, and a change counts as done only after the tests and the console say so.
